sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the import tests
sections.what: Loads the test tools, the import route handlers, and database helpers.
sections.why: Needed to call the routes and prepare the database.

sections.name: params
sections.title: Case parameter helper
sections.what: Builds the parameter shape the route handlers expect for a case id.
sections.why: Same reason as the other route tests.

sections.name: request
sections.title: Request helper and clean-up
sections.what: Builds a POST request with an optional record id. Before each test, it initializes the database and clears existing records for the two demo cases. After each test, it resets the database.
sections.why: Each test needs a known, clean starting state.
sections.watch_out: The cleanup names a database table directly, so renaming that table breaks every test.

sections.name: official record import and read API (part 1)
sections.title: Empty read and hero import tests
sections.what: Checks an empty read and an unknown case, then checks that importing the hero record returns the expected parcel numbers, recorded area, and non-authoritative flag.
sections.why: Confirms the record is traceable and labeled as not official.
sections.watch_out: The expected parcel numbers and area are fixed to the seed data.

sections.name: official record import and read API (part 2)
sections.title: Isolation and repeat import setup
sections.what: Checks that the hero import and the control import do not leak into each other, and begins the repeat import test by importing the same record twice.
sections.watch_out: The repeated-import check depends on the second assertion block below, so both halves must stay together.

sections.name: official record import and read API (part 3)
sections.title: Repeat import and error response checks
sections.what: Checks that a repeat import is flagged as already imported and that only one record remains. Then checks that malformed, unknown, and mismatched imports return 400, 404, 409, and 404.
sections.why: Confirms repeat imports do not duplicate and bad requests are refused with clear codes.
sections.watch_out: The 409 for a mismatch must stay in line with the route, or the test will fail.

summary: Tests importing official-style synthetic land records into a case, reading them back, and refusing unknown or mismatched imports.
purpose: Protects the official record import feature.
why: Likely reason: keeps imported records clearly marked as not authoritative and tied to the correct case.
how: Before each test, clears the record rows for the two demo cases. Tests then cover an empty read and an unknown case, a hero import with its traceability fields, isolation between hero and control imports, repeated import treated as one record, and bad, unknown, or mismatched imports returning 400, 404, 409, and 404.
inputs: Synthetic official record ids and demo case ids.
outputs: Pass or fail for each test.
risks: The cleanup deletes rows from a database table directly with SQL, bypassing the app's own logic. This is acceptable for tests but would be unsafe in real use.
debug: If import tests fail, check the official record service's identity matching and the record table.
